data.text/markdown:
Bloom tuning — feature C

Frame: docs/assets/flow-pulses/05-motion-on-a.png   1600×1001 This is a real capture of the map with ribbons (B) and flow pulses (A) live. The pipeline below is the same one the shader will run.

Dials

  only pixels brighter than this bloom at all. Too low and the whole map hazes over; too high and only the pulse crests glow.   how abruptly the threshold bites. 0 is a hard cutoff and tends to make bloom pop on and off as the pulse travels.   how far the light spreads.   each pass re-blurs the result — cheaper than one huge radius and gives a softer falloff.   how much of the blur is added back on top.   blur is done at reduced resolution on the GPU because it is the expensive step; this shows what that costs you visually.

Result

1.8% of the frame passes the bright-pass. Under ~1% and the bloom is invisible; over ~15% and the map starts to look foggy rather than lit.

data.text/markdown:
Constants for the shader

Paste these into mapRenderer.ts when the look is right: 
// bright-pass
const float BLOOM_THRESHOLD = 0.34;
const float BLOOM_KNEE      = 0.12;
// blur
const float BLOOM_SIGMA     = 7.0;   // px, at full res
const int   BLOOM_PASSES    = 2;
const int   BLOOM_DOWNSAMPLE= 2;
// composite
const float BLOOM_INTENSITY = 1.15;
Suggested starting point if you want somewhere to return to: threshold 0.34, knee 0.12, σ 7.0, 2 passes, downsample 2, intensity 1.15.
